title: A worker records a decision; the master finds out
trigger: a worker decides something while the master is busy elsewhere, and nobody sends a message

steps.text: Calls node_create (kind decision) with its actor name.
The worker's own MCP server validates the write and opens a transaction.

check.note: views.node_create validates kind/title/status/state/attrs then with tx(con), views.py:90-99@83a5621; each MCP server process holds its own connection (server.py:23-27).

steps.text: BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write lock: any other session's write waits (busy_timeout), so writes are serial.

check.note: tx() BEGIN IMMEDIATE db.py:241@83a5621; busy_timeout=10000 (db.py:219), so waits are bounded at 10 s.

steps.text: The node row is inserted, with attrs.created_by = the worker.

check.note: insert_node INSERT INTO node db.py:315-325@83a5621; node_create passes attrs.created_by=actor (views.py:111).

steps.text: The same transaction writes an attributed change row.

check.note: log_change INSERT INTO change(at, actor, node_id, what) db.py:373@83a5621, inside node_create tx (views.py:112).

steps.text: Later, the master calls changes_since with the `now` from its last call.

check.note: MCP changes_since(since, ...) server.py:120-124@83a5621; docstring: pass previous `now`.

steps.text: The master's own server reads change rows after that time: the worker's write is visible because both connect to the same file.

check.note: SELECT * FROM change WHERE at > since, views.py:73-82@83a5621; same file via DB_PATH, WAL.

steps.text: It opens the new node with node_get and acts on it.

check.note: node_get -> node_detail (node, parent, children, edges), server.py:92-95@83a5621.
